Entries.SourceTerm: 即今休去便休去，欲覓了時無了時

Senses.PreferredTarget: If you can stop right now, stop right now; if you seek a time when it will be finished, no such time will come
AlternateTargets: Rest from it now; looking for a later day of completion will never end
SearchAliases: stop now no time of final completion Chan
rest now do not seek later end Zen
Senses.Note: The first half tells the listener to stop now; the second says that searching for a later time when everything is finished will not bring that time. Linye, Fangrong, Yikui, Xiaotang, and Tanfang use the pair in separate present talks. Their contexts press the listener toward what can be done immediately instead of setting up another future milestone.

Occurrences.Kwic: 主丈云：德山來也。遂置主丈處，世界如虗空，如蓮花不著水，心清淨超於彼。上堂。諸佛出世，祖師西來，早是不著便。三百五百，成群作隊，說黃道黑，指東畫西，野狐見解。拈主丈云：觀世音將錢買胡餅，放下手却是饅頭。靠主丈下座。上堂，舉：僧問趙州：如何是毗盧頂相？州云：自小出家，不曾眼華。忽有人問青山：如何是毗盧頂相？只對他道：繅成白雪桑重綠，割盡黃雲稻正青。且道與趙州是同是別？仰山了堂首座至，上堂：摩訶衍法，離四句，絕百非。崇因寺裏打鼓，上堂：隊隊衲僧來，隊隊衲僧去。喝！上堂，舉：僧問投子：枯木裏還有龍吟也無？投子云：我道汝髑髏裏獅子吼。師頌云：枯木老龍吟，髑髏師子吼；九九八十一，面南看北斗。解夏，小參。諸方有為人句，青山無為人句；諸方有殺人刀、活人劒，青山無殺人刀、活人劒；諸方有結、有解，青山無結、無解。是汝諸人向者裏立，地皮下還有血麼？若約山僧看來，三世諸佛不如你、六代祖師不如你、天下老和尚不如你。復云：不用思量不用疑，目前法法是全提，即今休去便休去，欲覓了時無了時。久立，珍重。上堂。明暗有去來，虗空無動轉。萬象既歷然，一真自忌鑑。竪拂，釋迦老子在拂子頭上說大法要。放拂，云：見汝諸人不會，走人露柱裏去也。喝一喝，下座。上堂。古德道，蕪湖蕪湖見，當塗當塗見。八月十五夜，恰似沒柄扇。美則美矣，似則未似。青山則不然，開眼開眼見，合眼合眼見。蕪湖與當塗，不出廣寒殿。喝一喝，下座。上堂。五祖道：祖師說不著，佛眼覰不見。四面老婆心，為君通一線。青山道：開口便道著，開眼便󳬇見。青山老婆心，何曾通一線？便下座。上堂：教中道，一人發真歸源，十方虗空悉皆消殞。佛殿𡎺著你鼻孔，鐘樓塞破你腦門。作麼生得相應去？喝一喝。上堂。欲識佛性義，當觀時節因緣。時節若至，其理自彰。靜夜鐘聲，隨扣擊以無虧；澄潭月影，觸波瀾而不散。恁麼也得，不恁麼也得，恁麼不恁麼總得。擊拂子：師子不食鵰，殘俊鷹那打死兔。下座。冬至，小參。釋迦老子眼裏無筋，達磨大師皮下無血，諸人只知從冬數九、臘前三白，不知昨夜老梅向南一枝凍折。以拂子擊禪床一下，復云：少室峰前金鳳舞，曹溪路上玉雞啼，青山今夜打參鼓，留得閒僧立片時。請西洲首座上堂，卷舒立方外乾坤，縱橫挂域中日月，首座打板坐禪，長老舉揚宗旨，寒山拾得掃地裝香，彌勒釋迦搬柴運水。便下座。元宵，進退

ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 即今休去便休去，欲覓了時無了時

Senses.Explanation: The saying opposes stopping now to waiting for a final later moment. Linye and Fangrong put the pair after urging a direct response in the present assembly. Yikui, Xiaotang, and Tanfang likewise resist postponing the matter to a future finish.

Entries.SourceTerm: 即今休去便休去，若覓了時無了時

Senses.PreferredTarget: If you can stop now, stop now; if you seek a time when it is done, no such time will come
AlternateTargets: Rest from it right now; looking for a later finish will never finish
SearchAliases: stop now no time to finish later
if you seek completion no completion time
Senses.Note: The older line presses for stopping now: someone who waits to find a later moment when the work is finished will never find that moment. Yuanwu uses it after years of sustained inquiry, and Tian'an quotes it while warning against treating awakening as a debt with a scheduled payoff. Yinyuan gives it when a monk leaves the hall; Azi uses it in a memorial address about life and death.

Senses.Explanation: ‘If you can stop now, stop now; if you seek a time when it is done, no such time will come’ presses for a present release. Masters apply it to the wish for a final, scheduled state that can always be put off until later. Yuanwu cites the line after describing years of inquiry and release of its props. Tian'an gives it after warning that awakening cannot be repaid or achieved as a dated debt. Yinyuan says it when a monk exits after a challenge about the first gate. Chaozong quotes it to a lay patron and asks why he should wait any longer. Azi gives the line at a memorial after asking where the deceased now abides, then says one further unsaid line still remains.

Senses.Explanation: This very mind is this very buddha: a recorded saying, question, quoted case, and the first member of a recurring contrast with 'not mind, not buddha' (非心非佛). In the exact wording (即心即佛), the first 'this very' (即) identifies mind, and the second identifies buddha. In the record of Huineng and Fahai, Fahai asks for an explanation of 'this mind is this buddha' (即心即佛願垂指喻); Huineng answers by pairing 'the preceding thought not arising is this mind' (前念不生即心) with 'the following thought not ceasing is this buddha' (後念不滅即佛), then 'forming every characteristic is this mind' (成一切相即心) with 'leaving every characteristic is this buddha' (離一切相即佛). In Mazu's recorded exchange, when asked why he says it, he answers, 'to stop a small child crying' (為止小兒啼); when asked what happens after the crying stops, he says, 'not mind, not buddha' (非心非佛). Damei Fachang is later quoted saying that Mazu told him 'this mind is this buddha' and that, whatever Mazu now says about 'not mind, not buddha,' he retains the former words. Later masters also ask 'How is it when this mind is this buddha?' (即心即佛時如何) and place the phrase beside 'not mind, not buddha' and 'not mind, not buddha, not a thing' (不是心不是佛不是物). Chushi Fanqi pairs the phrase with ‘not mind, not buddha’ before dismissing both with a marketplace saying. Danxia Dangui calls the negative formula a note on the positive one. In Chaozong Tongren's hall, an unnamed monk asks how both can stand and Chaozong tells him to keep running between two ends. These witnesses preserve one quoted formulation while showing three sharply different public uses.

Senses.Note: The pair joins 'mind itself is Buddha' to 'neither mind nor Buddha.' Yezhu, Jie'an, Yunwai, Qiran, Lianfeng, and Shanyi use both halves together in separate current sermons or verses. Staff gestures, verse, and questions following the pair make the juxtaposition a live test. Both component slogans have public headwords, but the linked contradiction is the distinct work of this full saying.

Senses.Explanation: The formula identifies this very mind with Buddha, yet the records present that identification as an answer, an instruction, and wording whose implications speakers continue to test. Mazu Daoyi answers Damei Fachang’s question “what is Buddha?” with “this very mind is Buddha” (即心是佛). Sikong Benjing pairs seeking Buddha with “this very mind is Buddha” and seeking the way with “no-mind is the way,” then explains that Buddha is awakened through mind and mind is made manifest by Buddha. Huangbo Xiyun says no particle of teaching is obtainable apart from the one mind and immediately states the formula, criticizing a second mind raised upon mind to seek Buddha outside. Daodu describes hearing the phrase, trusting it, and allowing no other direction. In Dahui Zonggao’s retelling, Damei retains “here I have only this very mind is Buddha” against Mazu’s later wording. Dahui himself states “this very mind is Buddha; there is no other Buddha,” reverses it as Buddha being mind, and continues by denying that mind belongs to spatial positions or Buddha to temporal positions. Thus the formula can answer, identify, awaken confidence, and be defended against a competing formulation; its force depends on the speaking turn rather than the bare identity syntax alone.

Senses.PreferredTarget: This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing; no further sound or form can be presented to you
AlternateTargets: In this seeing and hearing there is no fixed seeing or hearing; nothing else of sound and form can be shown
SearchAliases: this seeing hearing is not seeing hearing
no further sound or form to show
Senses.Note: The first clause turns ordinary seeing and hearing back on themselves. The second refuses to supply another sound or form as an object to seize. Several masters strike a board, raise a staff, or ask whether the assembly sees and hears, then speak this pair as the live test. Other present uses put it into a verse or conclusion. The line belongs to a longer four-clause verse in several sources, but these nine records each put the first pair to work in their own encounter.

Occurrences.Kwic: 大海，轉入轉深，直到脩證不立、人法兩忘，直須更進一步，則知海底飛紅塵，山頭翻白浪。」僧問：「『海底飛紅塵，山頭翻白浪』，是阿誰境界？」師云：「問在答處。」進云：「『煩惱海中為雨露』又作麼生？」師云：「答在問處。」進云：「吾師恁麼話，慣賣死貓頭。」師云：「一般冷色空山裏，霜葉雖紅不是春。」桂庭居士設茶請示眾。「靜夜霜鴻天外過，圓通筵上幾禪和？聲消聞脫渾無際，誰謂觀音在普陀？大眾要知：〈普門品〉人人具有。所以道『應以佛身得度者，即現佛身而為說法；應以菩薩身得度者，即現菩薩身而為說法；應以居士等身得度者，即現居士等身而為說法。』雖則現身可知，且道法如何說？即如雞鳴清曉、犬吠黃昏，事存函蓋，理應箭鋒。又如磬出雲衢，歌來漁浦，醒迷途之幽夢、啟靜慮之玄門，妙在渾忘管帶，不立功勛。所以道：將聞持佛，佛何不自聞？聞蓋聞理，既妙見性亦玄然。理固如是，且道事作麼生？秪如今夜桂庭居士聞此象田安般若期，特特入山設茶供眾，又合將何酬他則是？」良久，云：「即此見聞非見聞，無餘聲色可呈君。」爾策居士設茶請示眾。「古鏡埋塵黑似漆，左揩右磨光赫奕，懸向虛空炤膽寒，偷心管教一時息。大眾！要見古鏡麼？」以如意畫圓相，云：「應如是知、如是見、如是信解，莫生法相。倘有個漢出來道：『法相生也。』便向他道：『應如是知、如是見、如是信解，莫生法相。』所以古德道：『須參活句，莫參死句。』若向活句中薦得，可與佛祖為師；向死句中薦得，自救不了。」乃舉：「雲居舜老夫少時在洞山聰會下，一日乞食鄂渚，有居士問舜云：『古鏡未磨時如何？』舜云：『黑如漆。』又問：『磨後如何？』舜云：『炤天炤地。』居士笑云：『上人不是洞山來耶？』舜默慚，馳歸，舉似聰，聰代前語：『此去漢陽不遠。』又代後語：『黃鶴樓前鸚鵡洲。』舜悟其旨。今夜居士若問山僧：『古鏡未磨時如何？』則向他道：『門前水一溪。』『磨後如何？』便道：『屋後山萬層。』居士若向這裏會得，始知本有光明炤天炤地，不孤今夜設茶；其或未然，大須策起眉毛好。」僧問：「古鏡當空，胡來胡現、漢來漢現，胡漢不來時，又作麼生現？」師云：「喫茶也未？」進云：「露滴松枝翠，青山絕點埃。」師云：「喫茶莫道渴。」進云：「恁麼則『慣捉龍頭擒虎尾，無名山上顯雲雷』？」師云：「閑言語。」僧問：「人人有面古鏡，且道如意還有古鏡也無

Occurrences.Kwic: 堂那一通。過白雲寺贈蒼白老宿過白雲寺贈蒼白老宿僧居雲裏寺居山，徑幾曲兮谿幾灣，就此不知三伏暑，蒼蒼別是一人間。山居山居三箇芋頭品字煨，地爐香熟出寒灰。飽餐便是諸天供，門外從教紫詔來。避秦何處可尋山？縛箇茅蓬偷得閑。自住此間忘管待，竹門雖設未曾關。悼無著首座悼無著首座選佛場中第一人，名同昆季與天親。欲回兜率白椎去，棄卻空華夢裏身。真讚真讚者箇山巒，手卓拄杖；半風半顛，佛祖不讓。身栖海底，意在天上；黃檗山中，被人讚謗。楞伽峰頂，飲毒無量；偶到竹陽，撞著空相。奇筆丹青，圖醜模樣；呼而無聲，觀之有狀。諸狀既空，真亦是妄；無德可稱，寫之誰望？不如扯碎，分身萬嶂；免遺後世，罵我老象。腳蹋紅鞋，風流和尚；謹白諸人，莫要供養。佛事佛事太平挂板太平挂板「太平寺裏，新條初唱；選佛場中，舊令重嚴。金鐘震，千古不墜之洪音；玉板敲，萬劫長鳴之佳韻。擊遍擊，山河起舞；吼遍吼，大地春生。綱維規範，耳目叢林。」遂豎槌，云：「大眾見麼？」擊一下，云：「大眾聞麼？即此見聞非見聞，無餘聲色可呈君。」擲下槌，云：「箇中若了原無事，體用何妨分不分？」中慶挂板中慶挂板「靈質英苗，乘風響應，迥示人天，全提正令。」乃擊一下，云：「橫敲迸出千嵒月，驚起泥牛走碧空。」擲下槌，云：「大眾見麼？玉板晝鳴翻古調，金鐘夜吼轉新腔。」喝一喝，遂挂。為無學監院火為無學監院火「關中主，主中關，一把钁頭不離山，欲賣趙州茶味別，十年開種白雲間。且道即今向甚麼處去？觔斗一翻三界外，丙丁童子笑憨憨。」為片雪禪人火為片雪禪人火「樹下問吾生死訣，未曾一句向渠說，今日分明舉似伊，烈燄堆頭飛片雪。」為悟道行者火為悟道行者火「今日也忙忙，明日也忙忙。忙吹三昧火，腦後發圓光。且道煙消灰盡時還忙也無？忙到西方去，蓮臺九品香。」喝一喝。為無我老宿火為無我老宿火「乞法三村老比丘，修行年老愛風流，悄然欲返無生國，猶戴霜華白滿頭。且道無生國路頭在甚麼處？」乃攛下炬，云：「去。」象崖珽禪師語錄卷第四行狀象崖珽禪師行狀師諱性珽，字象崖，係福建福州府福清縣陳氏子，母林氏。師生而穎異，長且敦敏，寡言笑，務實學。一日，同舅氏遊吳山寺隨喜，偶閱《禪宗正脈》，至「古德上堂，拈拄杖云：『法身無相而今現，形似打動自家底。』」意欲出塵，即歸，告辭二親，久乃許之，投長樂常熙福公薙髮，是年十九歲

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 眾會麼？一般清意味，料得少人知。若真師子兒，不入他群隊。提持佛祖命脈，開張向上綱宗，移星轉斗，緯地經天，橫衝直撞，左右逢原，向肉案頭展具，酒樓上闖席，憨布袋十字街等人，豐干老方丈中養虎，袈裟裏艸鞋，赤腳下桐城，得大自在。如風奮迅三昧，所以測識他不得，名目他不得，趨向他不得，比擬他不得。如水中木，不住此岸，不住彼岸，不著中流，順流而入薩婆若海、三昧海、智慧海、福德海、壽量海、神通光明海。此也是你本有底，山僧到這裏添減他一絲毫不得。適有一事與諸人商量，僧問趙州：『至道無難，唯嫌揀擇。豈不是時人窠臼？』州云：『曾有人問老僧，直得五年分疏不下。』」拈拄杖卓一下橫几上，乃屈指云：「一祖摩訶迦葉，一祖阿難，三祖商那和脩，四祖優波鞠多。」喝一喝云：「若不喝住，數到明朝。」擿拄杖顧左右云：「漆桶不快。」上堂。「密室深閨不見人，縱然桃李未逢春。偶來月下調絃管，隔院梅華照比鄰。」豎拂子云：「賊身已露。」上堂。拈拄杖云：「見麼？」卓一下，云：「聞麼？即此見聞非見聞，無餘聲色可呈君。」舉拄杖云：「此是體橫案上，云此是用。箇中若了全無事，體用何妨分不分？所以一句能該八萬門，說甚麼雲門胡餅？一機迥超生死路，又何須趙老清茶？若是懸照妖鏡，秉昆吾刀，坐斷十方，冶鑄古今，便見天平地成萬民樂業。諸仁者！不望你手段惡辣，在毒蛇頭上抓癢、猛虎口中分腥，但切莫向虛空中挖縫、頑石上栽華。今日好生底，向本位中去，鷺鷥腿，蜘蛛腰，緊峭艸鞋，結束將來，山僧當頭點你一棒，你也須知痛癢始得。」噓一聲云：「摘楊華，摘楊華，蘇嚧悉唎吽泮吒。」上堂。「遠山如黛，野水碧波清漾。斜橋隱隱，聽雞鳴村舍竹籬門巷。鷺鷥刷羽蘆汀，征雁數聲嘹亮，風中簫管短長，夜來月自凋桐上。政黃牛橘皮湯止渴，懶殘師芋香無樣。髮長藉艸坐南曛，白眼視公侯卿相。化山老僧、船子和尚，堪笑箇不唧溜漢，擯出院又罰饡飯。總不若今朝善信設伊蒲，管教你箇箇氣充腹脹，免使得窮廝煎、餓廝悵。喫飽了，經行似群蜚之鳥，打坐如土木之像。十洲春盡華凋殘，珊瑚枝頭紅日上。參！」上堂。「一切聲是佛聲，一切色是佛色。鐘沈露曉煙光澀，清唳蘆汀鴻雁集，落葉打寒窗殘燈。一夕天寬地廣箇閒人，攪動愁腸如織，誰相識？」上堂。「捏不成團，一池冰映水晶盤，放無著處，碧琉璃月冬青樹。鳴條之風，難為把捉。秦宮之火，誰敢棲

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 大海，轉入轉深，直到脩證不立、人法兩忘，直須更進一步，則知海底飛紅塵，山頭翻白浪。」僧問：「『海底飛紅塵，山頭翻白浪』，是阿誰境界？」師云：「問在答處。」進云：「『煩惱海中為雨露』又作麼生？」師云：「答在問處。」進云：「吾師恁麼話，慣賣死貓頭。」師云：「一般冷色空山裏，霜葉雖紅不是春。」桂庭居士設茶請示眾。「靜夜霜鴻天外過，圓通筵上幾禪和？聲消聞脫渾無際，誰謂觀音在普陀？大眾要知：〈普門品〉人人具有。所以道『應以佛身得度者，即現佛身而為說法；應以菩薩身得度者，即現菩薩身而為說法；應以居士等身得度者，即現居士等身而為說法。』雖則現身可知，且道法如何說？即如雞鳴清曉、犬吠黃昏，事存函蓋，理應箭鋒。又如磬出雲衢，歌來漁浦，醒迷途之幽夢、啟靜慮之玄門，妙在渾忘管帶，不立功勛。所以道：將聞持佛，佛何不自聞？聞蓋聞理，既妙見性亦玄然。理固如是，且道事作麼生？秪如今夜桂庭居士聞此象田安般若期，特特入山設茶供眾，又合將何酬他則是？」良久，云：「即此見聞非見聞，無餘聲色可呈君。」爾策居士設茶請示眾。「古鏡埋塵黑似漆，左揩右磨光赫奕，懸向虛空炤膽寒，偷心管教一時息。大眾！要見古鏡麼？」以如意畫圓相，云：「應如是知、如是見、如是信解，莫生法相。倘有個漢出來道：『法相生也。』便向他道：『應如是知、如是見、如是信解，莫生法相。』所以古德道：『須參活句，莫參死句。』若向活句中薦得，可與佛祖為師；向死句中薦得，自救不了。」乃舉：「雲居舜老夫少時在洞山聰會下，一日乞食鄂渚，有居士問舜云：『古鏡未磨時如何？』舜云：『黑如漆。』又問：『磨後如何？』舜云：『炤天炤地。』居士笑云：『上人不是洞山來耶？』舜默慚，馳歸，舉似聰，聰代前語：『此去漢陽不遠。』又代後語：『黃鶴樓前鸚鵡洲。』舜悟其旨。今夜居士若問山僧：『古鏡未磨時如何？』則向他道：『門前水一溪。』『磨後如何？』便道：『屋後山萬層。』居士若向這裏會得，始知本有光明炤天炤地，不孤今夜設茶；其或未然，大須策起眉毛好。」僧問：「古鏡當空，胡來胡現、漢來漢現，胡漢不來時，又作麼生現？」師云：「喫茶也未？」進云：「露滴松枝翠，青山絕點埃。」師云：「喫茶莫道渴。」進云：「恁麼則『慣捉龍頭擒虎尾，無名山上顯雲雷』？」師云：「閑言語。」僧問：「人人有面古鏡，且道如意還有古鏡也無

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 堂那一通。過白雲寺贈蒼白老宿過白雲寺贈蒼白老宿僧居雲裏寺居山，徑幾曲兮谿幾灣，就此不知三伏暑，蒼蒼別是一人間。山居山居三箇芋頭品字煨，地爐香熟出寒灰。飽餐便是諸天供，門外從教紫詔來。避秦何處可尋山？縛箇茅蓬偷得閑。自住此間忘管待，竹門雖設未曾關。悼無著首座悼無著首座選佛場中第一人，名同昆季與天親。欲回兜率白椎去，棄卻空華夢裏身。真讚真讚者箇山巒，手卓拄杖；半風半顛，佛祖不讓。身栖海底，意在天上；黃檗山中，被人讚謗。楞伽峰頂，飲毒無量；偶到竹陽，撞著空相。奇筆丹青，圖醜模樣；呼而無聲，觀之有狀。諸狀既空，真亦是妄；無德可稱，寫之誰望？不如扯碎，分身萬嶂；免遺後世，罵我老象。腳蹋紅鞋，風流和尚；謹白諸人，莫要供養。佛事佛事太平挂板太平挂板「太平寺裏，新條初唱；選佛場中，舊令重嚴。金鐘震，千古不墜之洪音；玉板敲，萬劫長鳴之佳韻。擊遍擊，山河起舞；吼遍吼，大地春生。綱維規範，耳目叢林。」遂豎槌，云：「大眾見麼？」擊一下，云：「大眾聞麼？即此見聞非見聞，無餘聲色可呈君。」擲下槌，云：「箇中若了原無事，體用何妨分不分？」中慶挂板中慶挂板「靈質英苗，乘風響應，迥示人天，全提正令。」乃擊一下，云：「橫敲迸出千嵒月，驚起泥牛走碧空。」擲下槌，云：「大眾見麼？玉板晝鳴翻古調，金鐘夜吼轉新腔。」喝一喝，遂挂。為無學監院火為無學監院火「關中主，主中關，一把钁頭不離山，欲賣趙州茶味別，十年開種白雲間。且道即今向甚麼處去？觔斗一翻三界外，丙丁童子笑憨憨。」為片雪禪人火為片雪禪人火「樹下問吾生死訣，未曾一句向渠說，今日分明舉似伊，烈燄堆頭飛片雪。」為悟道行者火為悟道行者火「今日也忙忙，明日也忙忙。忙吹三昧火，腦後發圓光。且道煙消灰盡時還忙也無？忙到西方去，蓮臺九品香。」喝一喝。為無我老宿火為無我老宿火「乞法三村老比丘，修行年老愛風流，悄然欲返無生國，猶戴霜華白滿頭。且道無生國路頭在甚麼處？」乃攛下炬，云：「去。」象崖珽禪師語錄卷第四行狀象崖珽禪師行狀師諱性珽，字象崖，係福建福州府福清縣陳氏子，母林氏。師生而穎異，長且敦敏，寡言笑，務實學。一日，同舅氏遊吳山寺隨喜，偶閱《禪宗正脈》，至「古德上堂，拈拄杖云：『法身無相而今現，形似打動自家底。』」意欲出塵，即歸，告辭二親，久乃許之，投長樂常熙福公薙髮，是年十九歲

Senses.Explanation: The demonstrative this points to the present act of seeing and hearing. The negation denies that this act can be pinned down as a fixed object. The second clause offers no other sound or form to stand in its place.

Senses.PreferredTarget: Clarify mind through forms; show principle by way of things
SearchAliases: clarify mind through forms; show principle by way of things
Senses.Note: The saying proposes that forms clarify mind and things reveal principle. Qingyu turns to donkey and dog sounds; Wanru moves from egrets and orioles to impossible scenes. Linye quotes the phrase, raises a whisk, points to a censer, and asks what mind and principle would be there. Wuzhun and Yuejian revisit a whisk case with different replies. These uses test whether the formula guides direct recognition or only repeats an explanation.

Senses.Explanation: Nüwa is the pre-Zen culture figure whom masters invoke as the woman who smelted stones to repair the broken sky. Wansong pairs her sky-repair with Yu’s opening of mountains and seas while praising the handling of Nanquan’s cat case; later addresses compare construction, restoration, or stone-working with her repair. Zen defines her here through that repeatedly serviceable image, not a freestanding mythology.

Senses.Explanation: Yunmen’s saying places countless dead on level ground and contrasts them with one who passes through the thorn forest. Doushuai and Xiatang explicitly raise Yunmen’s line; Tiantong, Liao’an, and Tian’an use the level-ground wording in their own addresses or comments.

Entries.SourceTerm: 平地上死人無數，過得荊棘林是好手

Senses.PreferredTarget: Countless die on level ground; one who gets through the thorn thicket has skill
SearchAliases: countless die on level ground; one who gets through the thorn thicket has skill
Senses.Note: Yunmen warns that many die on level ground, while getting through a thorn thicket takes skill. Huitang asks a monk how he would pass it; Duanqiao makes the line into a battle scene. Yuan'an uses it against resting at a quiet window, and Huiyue asks who could pass if the traveller is already dead. Qingyu voices it at a memorial before testing whether even avoiding two extremes becomes another resting place. The contrast exposes the risk in an apparently easy footing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 處？僧曰：和尚話墮也。師曰：爾十二時中向什麼處安身立命？僧無對。師曰：却來者裏謾我。以拂子打出。舉：長慶與保福商量，教中道：如來唯一說，無二說。保福問：作麼生是如來說？長慶曰：聾人爭得聞？福曰：情知老兄向第二頭裏接人。慶却問福：作麼生是如來說？福曰：齋後未喫茶。師問僧：只如長慶道：聾人爭得聞。如何却落第二頭？僧曰：聾人爭得聞？師曰：無繩自縛漢。我更問爾：如來唯一說，作麼生見得一底道理？僧瞪目而視。師曰：比來問一，爾却答二。舉雲門有時道：平地上死人無數，過得荊棘林是好手。師問僧：今時所見，多有此色，總活埋在者裏。是爾如何道得過却荊棘林？僧提起坐具：我者箇是八尺布作。師曰：不信道。舉：夾山曰：百草頭上薦取老僧，閙市裡識取天子。師拈起拂子看：拂子變成夾山老子，出來見麼？僧曰：謝和尚指示。師曰：見爾不顧，如今却入露柱中去也。舉寒山道：欲得安身處，寒山可長保。微風吹幽松，近聽聲愈好。下有斑白人，諵諵讀黃老。十年歸不得，忘却來時道。僧問：作麼生是來時道？師指香爐曰：看寒山來也，見麼？僧曰：好箇香爐。師曰：慚愧。

Occurrences.Kwic: 斗。卓拄杖。佛涅槃，上堂。今朝二月十五，萬象森羅起舞。世尊入般涅槃，壽山擊動法鼓。大眾若道世尊滅度，是謗佛；若道世尊不滅度，是謗法；若道諸人不會此理，是謗僧。謗佛、謗法、謗僧，合入無間地獄。到者裡，出身猶可易，脫體道應難。直須高高峯頂立不露頂，深深海底行不濕脚，然後荊棘林裡坐、荊棘林裡臥，開佛知見、示佛知見，令諸眾生悟佛知見、入佛知見。喝！知見立知，即無明本；知見無見，斯即涅槃。拍禪床，云：一把柳絲收不得，和煙搭在玉闌干。開山忌，上堂：平地上死人無數，過得荊棘林是好手。今朝三月十五，正是夏前春後。饒你不住兩頭，當處也成窠臼。拈拄杖：即今慧靜禪師向拄杖頭上，吹無孔笛，鼓沒絃琴。非唯戞玉鏗金，直是移星換斗。卓拄杖，喝一喝。上堂。師子吼，無畏說，百獸聞之皆腦裂，香象奔波失却威，天龍寂聽生欣悅。左擊拂子云：者箇不是師子吼。右擊拂子云：者箇不是無畏說。諸人耳在一聲中，一聲徧在諸人耳，不是寂聽生欣悅。恁麼恁麼，卷舒立方外乾坤；不恁麼不恁麼，縱橫掛域中日月。恁麼中有不恁麼，不恁麼中却恁麼。下座。詣大佛殿啟建天壽聖

Senses.Explanation: The “ordinary mind” is repeatedly named as the way, but the records contest what counts as ordinary rather than equating it with unexamined habit. In the Zhaozhou–Nanquan exchange, Nanquan Puyuan answers “the ordinary mind is the way” (平常心是道), then says that aiming toward it already departs from it. Mazu Daoyi gives an explicit account: ordinary mind has no contrivance, right or wrong, grasping or rejecting, annihilation or permanence, ordinary or sage (無造作，無是非，無取捨，無斷常，無凡聖); walking, standing, sitting, lying down, and responding to circumstances are all the way. Zhongfeng Mingben warns that the ordinary mind belongs neither to knowing nor to intellectual understanding and that attempts to harmonize explanatory formulas with it become measurement by discriminating consciousness. Zhenjing Kewen criticizes taking “the whole ordinary mind is the way” as a final rule merely meaning that each conventional thing is just itself. Zhuanyu Guanheng deliberately extends ordinary mind through relations between spouses, siblings, parents and children, friends, ruler and minister, and seasonal change, then says that actually pointing it out within those relations remains difficult. Yuanwu Keqin describes meeting meals and tea as they come while according with ordinary mind, explicitly adding that views of buddha and teaching do not arise. The term therefore ranges across a case answer, direct characterization, ordinary activity, social application, and warnings against turning ordinariness into a settled conceptual formula.

Senses.Note: Linji says the matter is ordinary and without an extra task, then names dressing, eating, and sleeping. Yunwai warns that taking his own teaching as mere nothing-to-do would miss it. Yuanwu says a person who has investigated thoroughly reaches ordinary ease, while cautioning against dead stillness. Dahui criticizes a reading that uses the phrase to avoid inquiry and reduce every answer to literal common sense. Wunian tells a correspondent to drop manufactured displays and answer when called. These uses distinguish living ease from a posture of passivity.

Senses.Explanation: To walk level into the blue sky is to advance into an otherwise unreachable height as easily as on flat ground. Liao'an Qingyu opposes it to being mud-covered, Tian'an Sheng grants it to whoever can give a turning word, and Muchen Daomin places it in a novice's tonsure verse. Liao'an also reverses the apparent opposition: the mud-covered condition contains the way of level walking into the sky, and level walking carries news of the mud-covered condition.

Senses.Explanation: All my life I have poured out my heart to people, yet they know me as though they did not know me. Baoning Renyong calls his own preceding disclosure a burial of the listeners, then follows it with this couplet. Baoning Renyong says it after declaring that his own preceding words have already buried his listeners, then lifts his staff and continues the address. Kuanan Jing, Shiwu Qinggong, Gulin Qingmao, and Chushi Fanqi reuse the same couplet in distinct addresses, repeatedly holding together complete disclosure and failed recognition.

Senses.Explanation: The wisdom of equality is one of the four transformed wisdoms named in the retained expositions. In a retreat-opening address, Wuzhun Shifan says that mind is like the realm of empty space and presents a teaching equal to empty space, where neither affirmation nor denial remains. He says that buddhas and patriarchs have transmitted this mind teaching to carry out the work of a buddha. He then makes that teaching the great monastery at Jingshan and says that throughout the ten directions, whether holy or ordinary, all dwell together in the wisdom of equality; he closes by raising and striking his staff.

Senses.Explanation: “Profoundly dim and obscure” describes what is deeply indistinct; its evaluation depends on the surrounding claim. Hongzhi Zhengjue repeats the old wording that within the dim obscurity there is vitality; Yuanwu Keqin instead warns that reducing matters to blank nonexistence leaves one dimly and obscurely lost. The polarity changes, but the descriptive floor does not. Two independent present source uses deepen the existing two public witnesses: Buhui places the phrase in his own Lantern Festival hall verse, saying even dark obscurity is disclosed by the lamp of direct seeing. Miyin uses the phrase in his own verse to a practitioner, warning against passing the days in obscurity without resolving birth and death.

Senses.Note: Across the collected corpus the expression has 682 exact occurrences in 180 distinct works. Deployment inventory includes blow-verdict, direct instruction, question, spatial reversal, and the compound 'the matter under your heels' (腳跟下事). Family check with heel (腳跟), underfoot (腳下), on the spot (立地), one's own part (本分), thirty blows (三十棒), and atop the head (頭上) supports one spatial referent used in several interview acts. Literal and loaded uses were not split because the loaded use keeps the same deictic location rather than naming a different thing.

Senses.Explanation: The recorded formula 'right under your heels' locates what is immediately beneath one's stance and recurs in demands to inspect or recognize what lies there, in questions about it, and in appraisals and reversals. Chan interviews repeatedly turn this ordinary location back upon the person questioned. Poshan Haiming gives the appraisal 'right under your heels, thirty blows would be fitting.' Wuyi Yuanlai asks 'how deep is the water under your heels?', Sanshan Denglai directs a questioner to 'recognize it right under your heels,' and Juelang Daosheng answers a request for direct pointing with 'look clearly right under your heels.' The phrase also marks relative position in a public comparison: if the unnamed monastic can distinguish the kinds of leakage, Dongshan is under his heels; if not, he is under Dongshan's heels. A stock question asks about 'the matter under your heels' and receives 'putting a head atop your head.' The Chan-specific bend is consistent and observable: the spatial phrase becomes the immediate locus of an interviewer's demand, appraisal, or reversal, often contrasted with what the questioner seeks elsewhere or above. The texts do not supply a further object hidden beneath the feet, and neither does this entry.
